newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Thousands gather in Albanian town for new protest.
newsitem.headline: Thousands gather in Albanian town for new protest.

text.p: More than 10,000 demonstrators gathered in this southern Albanian town on Tuesday evening to protest against the government's handling of a series of collapsed investment schemes, eyewitnesses said.
A crowd of at least 5,000 protesters was on its way by foot from the town of Fier, some 35 km (20 miles) to the north, to join the protest, they said.
Security forces stayed away and the local police station, scene of violent clashes for the past two days that have claimed two lives, was virtually deserted.

Many people in this Adriatic port accuse Berisha's right-wing government of stealing money they placed in a local pyramid fund which went broke last week owing the estimated equivalent of $500 million.
Several opposition leaders were in the crowd gathered in in the main square, among them Neritan Ceka, leader of the Democratic Alliance of opposition parties.
"We have come to Vlore to establish a dialogue between the people and the government, to solve the economic crisis and later the political crisis," Ceka told the crowd.

The opposition demands the resignation of President Sali Berisha's government and blames him for the collapse of pyramid investment schemes with the life savings of hundreds of thousands of Albanians.
Around 30,000 people turned out for the funeral of one of the riot's victims earlier on Tuesday.
In the capital Tirana, parliament was due to vote on Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's proposal to declare a state of emergency in Vlore.
